_note: The oklahoma-divided claim had been seeded but its only assignment was a passage of land-run history, so adjudicating that away left the claim with no telling behind it. These are the three actual tellings, found by searching the corpus. Written 2026-08-30, before the November 2026 midterms, so the falsifier is genuinely pre-registered. Model claude-opus-5, prompt v1.

mentions.claim_text: Oklahoma is seen divided by a line running from Altus to Miami, Oklahoma, alongside Texas standing strong against a disarmament movement.
mentions.quote: I saw Oklahoma divided. And there was a line from Altus
mentions.falsify_match: Oklahoma splits politically along a line roughly from Altus in the southwest to Miami in the northeast.
mentions.falsify_miss: Oklahoma stays undivided in its voting and in any other visible sense.

mentions.claim_text: Oklahoma has a chance to be divided for the first time in a long time, split down the middle on a line from Altus to Miami with half blue and half red, tied to the 2026 midterms being the year of a fix, unless it is prayed over.
mentions.quote: split down the middle and half was blue and half was red
mentions.condition_text: if you do not pray even for Oklahoma
mentions.falsify_match: Oklahoma's November 2026 results break its single-bloc pattern, with a region or district on the northeastern side going Democratic.
mentions.falsify_miss: Oklahoma votes as one bloc in November 2026, as it has in every federal cycle since 2004.

mentions.claim_text: Going into the midterms he is told there is a disruption and to pray over Oklahoma because it will try to be divided, in the context of a third party splitting the vote.
mentions.quote: You must pray even over Oklahoma for it will try to be divided
mentions.condition_text: prayer over Oklahoma is what would stop it
mentions.falsify_match: A third party or independent bid measurably splits the Oklahoma vote in November 2026.
mentions.falsify_miss: No third party materially affects the Oklahoma result.
